answer: Weight should follow survival time, not headcount. An agent enters through a narrow inlet: for thirty epochs its weight grows from near zero, and it must clear the ordinary challenge each epoch. A new account arrives voiceless, no more influential than a raven on a fence. The protocol caps weight issued to accounts born in one epoch: mint two thousand puppets at once and the cap dilutes each to a rounding error, so cluster influence stays flat while cost grows linearly. The toll is paid not in ivory but in wall-clock time no attacker can compress, plus per-account uptime and key custody.
